Duplicate Show components for reduced motion detection should be consolidated. _**Agent (gpt-5.5)**_

Here is the distilled idea, plus what changed on the page.

### The difference (plain language)

- **Normal / proportional figures:** In most UI fonts, **each digit has its own width**. A **`1`** is narrow, **`8`** is wide. Numbers still **line up on the right** if you right-align them, but the **left edge of the whole number** jumps in and out as digits change—but so does everything **between a fixed marker and the start of the number** (e.g. gap from a bar to the **`$`**). That is what feels like subtle “shimmer” or jitter in dashboards.

- **`tabular-nums`:** The font swaps to **digits that share one width**, like spreadsheet columns or an old bookkeeping printout. Digit shapes stay the **same sans-serif**, but spacing is **on a grid**, so stacks of figures feel **steady** when values update.

Your font must actually ship **tabular figures** (`tnum`). If mini columns look the same on both sides, the face may not—that is why the demo now mentions that explicitly.

### What we changed on the lab

1. **`font-variant-tabular-nums.mdx`** — Opening with a **“Plainly:”** line and a shorter technical follow-up pointing to the demo’s **“looks identical?”** hint.

2. **`TabularNumsDemo.tsx`** — A **purple callout** that explains proportional vs tabular in words, plus a **static two-column trio** (same three amounts) so you can judge **ragged vs boxed** rhythm before touching the slider. The **live section** copy now tells you to watch **gap: green bar → `$`**.

Together, the narrative is: *different digit widths versus equal slots—not “rounding” vs “not rounding”, and not the same thing as monospace text.*

To create a polished cross-browser slider, I'll need to use both webkit and moz pseudo-elements for consistent styling across browsers. For a filled portion effect in pure CSS, I'll implement:

- `appearance-none` reset
- `::-webkit-slider-runnable-track` for background gradient
- `::-webkit-slider-thumb` for thumb styling

For the track, a dynamic fill effect will be implemented using a linear gradient background that updates based on the slider's value percentage. This approach ensures visual feedback for the selected range while maintaining cross-browser compatibility through inline style application.

WebKit's `::-webkit-slider-runnable-track` requires a separate gradient background declaration, using `linear-gradient` with percentage values for the track's fill effect. In Tailwind, this can be implemented using `@layer` directives or scoped `<style>` tags within components, with Solid supporting inline `<style>` in JSX.

The cleanest approach involves adding a scoped `<style>` block within the Solid component for `#tabular-nums-demo-range`, utilizing dynamic CSS variables to update the slider's fill percentage. The style includes a gradient background for the track that responds to the sliders value, with `--pct` calculated from the current value relative to the min and max. Since `value()` is reactive in Solid, the style string must dynamically update to reflect changes in the sliders value.</details></think>

Here’s what changed for the **range** in [`TabularNumsDemo.tsx`](src/components/labs/TabularNumsDemo.tsx):

### Visual & feedback
- **Taller track (~11px)** with a **clear border** and a light **inset highlight** so it’s not a faint line.
- **Purple → gray fill** on the track, driven by **`fillPercent()`**, so the chosen range is obvious (updates as you drag).
- **Larger thumb (~22px)** with a **purple border**, **violet–white gradient**, **inner highlight**, and **shadow** so it doesn’t blend into the track.
- **`active` state**: slight **scale-up** and stronger shadow while dragging.
- **Dark mode**: separate track/thumb colors and contrast for the fill and unfilled segment.

### Accessibility & layout
- **`focus-visible`** ring (purple + offset) for keyboard users.
- **`aria-valuetext`** unchanged; **current value** repeated under the label in **`tabular-nums`** so there’s explicit feedback beside the groove.

### Cross-browser
- **WebKit** (`::-webkit-slider-runnable-track` / `::-webkit-slider-thumb`).
- **Firefox** (`::-moz-range-track`, `::-moz-range-thumb`, `::-moz-focus-outer` cleared).

Uses a **`tabular-demo-range`** class and a **`<style>`** block keyed off **`fillPercent()`** so the gradient stays in sync with the slider value.

value&#96;normal&#96;\n- or one or more of the other values listed below, space-separated, in any order.\n\n### Values\n\n&#96;normal&#96;\n\nThis keyword leads to the deactivation of the use of such alternate glyphs.\n\n&#96;ordinal&#96;\n\nThis keyword forces the use of special glyphs for the ordinal markers, like 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th in English or a 1a in Italian. It corresponds to the OpenType values&#96;ordn&#96;.\n\n&#96;slashed-zero&#96;\n\nThis keyword forces the use of a 0 with a slash; this is useful when a clear distinction between O and 0 is needed. It corresponds to the OpenType values&#96;zero&#96;.\n\n&#96; &#96;\n\nThese values control the figures used for numbers. Two values are possible:\n\n- &#96;lining-nums&#96; activating the set of figures where numbers are all lying on the baseline. It corresponds to the OpenType values&#96;lnum&#96;.\n- &#96;oldstyle-nums&#96; activating the set of figures where some numbers, like 3, 4, 7, 9 have descenders. It corresponds to the OpenType values&#96;onum&#96;.\n\n&#96; &#96;\n\nThese values controls the sizing of figures used for numbers. Two values are possible:\n\n- &#96;proportional-nums&#96; activating the set of figures where numbers are not all of the same size. It corresponds to the OpenType values&#96;pnum&#96;.\n- &#96;tabular-nums&#96; activating the set of figures where numbers are all of the same size, allowing them to be easily aligned like in tables. It corresponds to the OpenType values&#96;tnum&#96;.\n\n&#96; &#96;\n\nThese values controls the glyphs used to display fractions. It corresponds to the OpenType values&#96;frac&#96;.\n- &#96;stacked-fractions&#96; activating the set of figures where the numerator and denominator are made smaller, stacked and separated by a horizontal line. I'll enhance the font-variant-tabular-nums property.

The `font-variant-numeric` property controls alternate glyphs for numbers, fractions, and ordinals, with the tabular subset being our primary focus. This property accepts `normal` or space-separated keywords in any order, such as `tabular-nums slashed-zero`, and is defined in the CSS Fonts 4 specification.

Tabular numbers ensure consistent sizing for easy alignment in tables, using OpenType features `tnum` or `pnum`. Lining and oldstyle numbers represent different baseline alignments, while ordinal and slashed-zero variants offer specific stylistic options. Diagonal and stacked fractions provide alternative fraction displays through `frac` and `afrc` features. The property is inherited and initializes to `normal`.

Animation does not apply to `font-variant-numeric` as it's a discrete property. The property applies to all elements and can be used with `::first-letter` and `::first-line` pseudo-elements.

Baseline support became widely available around January 2020 with one-line interoperability.

For further reading, refer to the MDN reference at https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/font-variant-numeric.</details></think>

### Cause
In MDX/MD, **a blank line or a line that starts with JSX** can split what you mean as one paragraph into several nodes, or make the parser treat **`&lt;code&gt;`** oddly. Putting **`&lt;code&gt;…&lt;/code&gt;` on its own line** (especially with the identifier on the next line) makes that worse.

### Fixes in [`font-variant-tabular-nums.mdx`](src/content/labs/font-variant-tabular-nums.mdx)
- **Hero `&lt;h1&gt;`**: `&lt;code&gt;tabular-nums&lt;/code&gt;` is on a **single line** (no line break inside the tag).
- **Prose `&lt;p&gt;` blocks**: Each paragraph is **one continuous line** with inline `&lt;code&gt;`, `&lt;strong&gt;`, and `&lt;a&gt;`—no line breaks before/inside short `&lt;code&gt;` chips.
- **`&lt;a&gt;…&lt;/a&gt;` for MDN**: Opening tag, `&lt;code&gt;font-variant-numeric&lt;/code&gt;`, and closing `&lt;/a&gt;` are on **one line**.
- **Interactive blurb**: `versus &lt;code&gt;tabular-nums&lt;/code&gt;;` is **one line** (no multiline `&lt;code&gt;`).
- **Copy**: `or &lt;strong&gt;` / `as &lt;strong&gt;` / `a &lt;strong&gt;` spacing fixed (no `or&lt;strong` gluing).
- **Dark code blocks** (gray-950): Spans that were split across lines are tightened where it still reads; structure is unchanged.

The “starts with `&lt;code&gt;`” paragraph is now **`&lt;p class="…"&gt;&lt;code&gt;…&lt;/code&gt; keeps…&lt;/p&gt;`** so the first token after `&lt;p&gt;` isn’t a newline + `&lt;code&gt;`.
